results.corrected_extracted: The dummy condition was saline in 35 of the 36 healthy-volunteer studies and not reported in one. In the total-symptom analysis, two studies gave ketamine and placebo on the same day and 17 on different days (19 of its 25 studies), and the same-day design gave a larger pooled total-symptom effect (2.29, 95% CI 1.69 to 2.89, against 1.39, 1.12 to 1.66; P = .007 for the difference), which the authors, saying the reason is less clear, suggest could reflect unblinding or better control of day-to-day variation; for positive and negative symptoms the two designs did not differ significantly. The rating time was reported for 17 of the 36 studies and fell between 1 and 120 minutes after the infusion began. In the 4th Strengths and Limitations paragraph the authors state that further work is needed to characterise the dose-response relationship and the time course of these effects, so the review itself fixes no recovery time.

results.corrected_extracted: Where the review introduces the metabolite account in its main text, it names the evidence on both sides in one sentence: it states that the two hydroxynorketamines have been shown to produce antidepressant-relevant behaviour in rodents, citing its own authors' 2016 report and one independent study, and then, in the same parenthesis after 'but see', two independent studies, without saying what they found; their titles in its reference list report no antidepressant effect of (2R,6R)-HNK in a rat learned-helplessness model and (R)-ketamine as more potent and longer-lasting than (2R,6R)-HNK. The counter-evidence is named only there and its arguments are not described.
results.note: Review says 'have been shown', stronger than 'reported'. 'But see' does not say what the two studies found; by listed titles, one found no (2R,6R)-HNK effect in rats, the other (R)-ketamine more potent and longer-lasting. Both cited only here.
